resources.string: Reads on-screen text so Pinehold can step back out of the surfaces you chose to avoid, such as Shorts, Reels, WhatsApp Channels, or your own keywords. It only ever reads text: it never types, taps, or sends anything anywhere, and everything it sees stays on this phone.

This is the whole app, with two limits. It runs one session, and it shows you the block screen instead of taking the screen away from you. Sealed and Kiosk \u2014 the two modes that promise to hold the phone shut \u2014 are switched off here.
This is the demo\'s one session. Everything works as it does in the full version, except that a block is shown rather than enforced.
That was the demo\'s one session. Every screen, rule, schedule and task is still here to look at, and Test the block still previews your rules against whatever you open.
The demo\'s session is used up

Pinehold uses the Android AccessibilityService API solely to read on-screen text and window titles so it can detect when you enter distracting surfaces you chose to block (such as Shorts, Reels, WhatsApp Channels, blocked websites, or your own keywords) and step back out.

• All screen text is checked locally in memory and is never stored, logged, or transmitted off your device.
• Pinehold never modifies your settings or taps controls without your permission.
All session strengths (Sealed & Kiosk), Bedtime dimming, Place & Wi-Fi rules, Earn Mode, and Custom rules are unlocked on this device.
